answer.origin: NVIDIA Corporation company blog post dated 2026-07-01 (party statement, self-published), with a quoted Sharon AI CEO statement and NVIDIA's descriptions of Firmus and other AI clouds. No independent original source was supplied.
answer.note: NVIDIA's own 2026-07-01 blog post says it is introducing a model in which AI clouds procure NVIDIA infrastructure for AI-native, enterprise and ISV customers, supported by revenue-sharing and credit-support terms. NVIDIA says it would earn standard product revenue plus a share of cloud revenue on the supported capacity, which it describes as a recurring, usage-linked stream. If the model is adopted at scale, it would add a usage-linked revenue component on top of hardware sales and could widen NVIDIA's exposure to the financing and utilization risk of AI clouds, since credit support is part of the structure. The evidence is a company description of a program and its intended economics, not a reported result. The Firmus figures (360 MW and up to 170,000 NVIDIA GPUs) are an expected scale for a campus under construction, with no disclosed timing or contracted volume. The Sharon AI quote and the AI-native customer examples show intent to participate, not signed purchase commitments.
limitations: The revenue-share percentage, duration, credit-support size and the accounting treatment of both are not disclosed, so the size of the usage-linked stream cannot be estimated from this source.
No signed agreements with any named AI cloud are disclosed; participation is described as partnership or intent, so the number of participating clouds and their committed capacity are unknown.
The Firmus 360 MW and 170,000 GPU figures are an expected scale with no stated completion date or funding, and no NVIDIA purchase amount for that campus is given.
The source does not say whether the model has begun generating revenue or when its effect would appear in NVIDIA's reported results.
No historical records or prior NVIDIA disclosures on credit support or revenue sharing were supplied for comparison.
follow_up: Check NVIDIA's subsequent 10-Q or 10-K filings for disclosed credit-support guarantees, revenue-share arrangements or related receivables and contingent liabilities.
Check NVIDIA and partner announcements for named signed agreements, committed capacity and deployment dates for the Firmus and Sharon AI campuses.
Check whether NVIDIA reports any new revenue line or disclosure for cloud revenue shares in upcoming earnings materials.
